Change c0537. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): A frightful selfishness hurried me on, while my heart was poisoned with remorse.

1818 text: Think ye that the groans of Clerval were music to my ears? My heart was fashioned to be susceptible of love and sympathy; and, when wrenched by misery to vice and hatred, it did not endure the violence of the change without torture such as you cannot even imagine.

1831 text: Think you that the groans of Clerval were music to my ears? My heart was fashioned to be susceptible of love and sympathy; and, when wrenched by misery to vice and hatred, it did not endure the violence of the change, without torture such as you cannot even imagine.
